messages:
Elaine: Heads up — spotted a burst of spot preemptions in us-west-2b GPU pool, ~15% of spot capacity gone in last 10m. Thinking we should do a preemptive drain of low-priority spot nodes and swap routing to 2a/2c for latency-sensitive traffic.
Ramon: ACK. Can you share which nodepools are affected and estimate how much on-demand buffer we have? cc @infra-runner
Elaine: Affected nodepools: rw-gpu-spot-usw2b-1/2/3. On-demand headroom ~18% across the region but uneven per AZ. If we shift too much to 2a it'll saturate GPU queue for small models.
Aditi: Suggest throttling non-prod batch jobs first, then drain. Also want to pin KV caches for active chat sessions to avoid regen penalties during routing swap.
Jordan: Agree w/ Aditi. Also we should raise per-route rate limits temporarily for legacy model endpoints to prevent request fanout when instances move.
Elaine: Plan proposal:
1) mark rw-gpu-spot-usw2b-* nodes as schedulable:disabled (start cordon)
2) scale down batch nodepool + add on-demand capacity in 2a/2c
3) apply routing policy: prefer on-demand pools for routes with latency SLO < 200ms
4) pin KG caches for active sessions
5) monitor token-level latency and error counts
Ramon: Command snippets for step 1/2:
```
# cordon
kubectl cordon <node-name>
# move low-priority pods
kubectl -n infra get pods -l workload=batch -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# scale nodepool
gcloud container node-pools update rw-gpu-ondemand-usw2a --size=+8
```
Elaine: Also will kick off a quick canary: route 10% of traffic from a few critical routes to the new pools for 20m before full swap.
infra-runner: deploy-bot started drain job for rw-gpu-spot-usw2b-1 at 1780554330 — 12 pods evicted, 8 still terminating
deploy-bot: autoscaler triggered creation of 6 on-demand instances in us-west-2a (pool rw-gpu-ondemand-usw2a), est ready in ~3m :rocket:
Aditi: Watching LLM cache hit rate — if it drops >8% we should pause the canary. Also lower dynamic batching to reduce cold start tokens.
Jordan: I applied temporary route weights: us-west-2a=0.7, us-west-2c=0.2, us-west-2b=0.1 for critical-models via routing API
Elaine: Update — us-west-2b still seeing ~10% preemptions but drain completed on 2 of 3 nodepools. Latency on critical routes stable +12ms. Errors unchanged.
Ramon: Cost note — on-demand bump will cost ~+$6k/day if it stays for 24h. Recommend we re-evaluate after steady-state 1h.
Aditi: Reminder: schedule a quick job to pin heavy KV entries:
```
# pin session caches
redwood-cli cache pin --namespace sessions --selector active=true
```
infra-runner: rw-gpu-spot-usw2b-2 drain finished at 1780554620, 0 pods evicted remaining. Rebalancer moved 14 high-priority pods to ondemand pools.
Elaine: Canary complete (20m). No regressions, error rates within baseline. Proceeding to shift remaining 70% of latency-sensitive traffic to on-demand pools over next 10m.
Jordan: i'll keep the route weights rolling down for 10m windows. Alerting set if p50 > 230ms or error-rate +2x
deploy-bot: routing policy update applied at 1780555320
Ramon: post-action: schedule a capacity refill for spot pools and run a placement test. Also log this as a partial-AZ degrade event for the weekly ops sync.
Aditi: Filed a short runbook update — added steps for cache pin + batch throttle heuristics.
Elaine: Thanks team. Follow-ups: (1) cost analysis (Ramon), (2) runbook PR (Aditi), (3) customer-impact check on Dedicated tenants (Jordan). I'll close the thread once we confirm spot capacity is back to <5% preemptions.
Ramon: noted. I'll put a short blip in #incidents if Dedicated customers saw degraded throughput.
Elaine: closing updates: preemption rate in 2b back to 3% at 1780555940, ondemand scaledown scheduled in 45m. New on-demand cost spike estimate trimmed to ~$1.2k for the recovery window :thumbsup:
infra-runner: scaledown job queued for 1780558200
Elaine: great job everyone :tada:
